strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing uncertainty quantification in MLIPs with practical importance for active learning and error-aware simulations
Genuine computational efficiency advantage over Deep Ensembles: maintains single-model inference cost while providing calibrated uncertainties, important for high-throughput workflows
Comprehensive and honest experimental evaluation across three diverse tasks with strong baselines (Deep Ensembles, MC Dropout) and multiple uncertainty metrics (ECE, Spearman, NLL, CRPS)
Excellent reproducibility: detailed hyperparameters, architecture specifications, public datasets with links, algorithm pseudocode, and implementation details in appendices
Technically sound variational inference formulation with proper ELBO derivation and appropriate use of local reparameterization trick for scalability
Architecture-agnostic framework integrating with multiple MPNN variants (PaiNN, EGNN, ORB v3) across different system scales
weaknesses: Cannot be applied to important MLIP architectures (MACE, UMA) due to irreducible representation dimensions, severely limiting practical impact for the target domain despite architecture-agnostic claims

Equivariance preservation is not rigorous: individual forward passes break exact equivariance/invariance due to noise injection; claim that statistical moments remain equivariant is insufficiently justified for physical applications

Empirical improvements are marginal and inconsistent: ammonia energy overlaps within error bars (11.51±0.75 vs 11.71 ensemble), N-body EGNN shows ensemble superiority (0.057 vs 0.060), silica Spearman correlation significantly underperforms (0.602 vs 0.676). No significance tests provided

Requires substantial task-specific hyperparameter tuning undermining 'easy-to-use' claims: prior dropout varies dramatically (0.5→0.01 across tasks), KL weight λ varies by orders of magnitude (0.001-10), different clamping values per experiment, and new inference network design for each architecture
Limited algorithmic novelty: combines existing variational dropout (Kingma et al. 2015) and adaptive dropout (Coscia et al. 2025) without fundamental methodological advancement

Incomplete reproducibility: missing code URL despite statement that code is available; hyperparameter selection procedure unclear (validation-set tuning vs manual), no ablation studies on design choices

Statistical rigor issues: results reported with ±1 std but no hypothesis tests; some baseline comparisons lack error bars (Deep Ensemble NA entries); fairness concerns in fine-tuning comparison using different learning rates

Mixed uncertainty quantification results: good ECE for ammonia but poor Spearman correlation for silica (0.602 vs 0.676 ensemble), undermining reliability claims for active learning where correlation with error is critical

Limited evaluation scope: only three experiments, two chemistry tasks from same source (Tan et al. 2023); missing application to actual active learning pipelines despite motivation; no comparison with simpler UQ methods

Insufficient analysis of design choices: no ablation on inference network architecture, no sensitivity analysis for hyperparameters, variance decomposition (Eq. 14) discussed but not empirically analyzed

strengths: Addresses an important practical problem: uncertainty quantification in MLIPs with a computationally efficient single-model approach that outperforms Deep Ensembles in memory/computation while providing well-calibrated uncertainties

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across diverse tasks (N-body, ammonia OOD, silica glass, MATPES) with multiple metrics (MSE, NLL, CRPS, ECE, Spearman correlation) and proper statistical reporting (multiple seeds with error bars)

Technically sound framework with rigorous mathematical derivations: proper ELBO optimization, closed-form KL divergences, principled use of local reparameterization trick, and formal proofs of equivariance properties

Architecture-agnostic applicability: demonstrated on multiple architectures (GNN, EGNN, PaiNN, ORB v3) and applicable to both training from scratch and fine-tuning large pretrained models, enabling practical deployment

Practical efficiency advantages: maintains single-model inference cost (no overhead vs deterministic models) while providing uncertainty, achieving ~2× training cost vs ~5× for ensembles with competitive or better calibration than ensembles

Consistent improvements in uncertainty calibration: lower ECE than Deep Ensembles across tasks and strong correlation between predicted uncertainty and error (ρ ≈ 0.86), making uncertainties useful for downstream applications like active learning

Excellent presentation: clear writing, informative diagrams, comprehensive appendices with detailed proofs, algorithms, implementation details, hyperparameters, and architectural specifications supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Significant architectural limitations: local reparameterization trick breaks equivariance for models with irreducible representations, excluding important modern architectures (MACE, UMA), substantially reducing scope and applicability to state-of-the-art equivariant potentials

Inconsistent and often modest improvements over Deep Ensembles: EGNN case shows Deep Ensemble outperforming BLIP (0.057 vs 0.060 MSE), ammonia shows only ~1.7% energy improvement, and SiO2 shows marginal differences within error bars, weakening claims of consistent superiority

Limited technical novelty: core contribution adapts existing adaptive variational dropout from Coscia et al. (2025) to MLIPs—primarily an application rather than a methodological advance, reducing the fundamental scientific contribution

Hyperparameter sensitivity and unclear tuning procedures: prior dropout probability p and KL weight λ vary dramatically across experiments (p: 0.5→0.01, λ: 0.001→10) without clear guidance on selection; appears to require extensive task-specific tuning, limiting generalizability

Single Monte Carlo sample during training: using only one stochastic sample per iteration risks high-variance gradient estimates; no analysis of convergence properties, variance of gradients, or impact on optimization stability is provided

Incomplete baseline comparisons: Deep Ensemble results marked 'NA' for uncertainty in Table 1 (unclear if not computed or not reported), missing wall-clock time comparisons beyond FLOP analysis, no comparison to recent single-model UQ methods beyond MC Dropout

Independent factorization assumptions not validated: posterior factorization across layers and between message/update functions (Eq. 4) may be overly restrictive; no empirical analysis of whether independence assumptions hold or affect downstream performance

Prior choice lacks principled justification: zero-mean Gaussian prior motivated primarily by dropout interpretation rather than principled Bayesian reasoning; sensitivity to prior specification is unexplored
